assumptions.text: QuoteStore.update_quote must not raise StoreUnavailableError (or any other exception) in the scope of this task; behavior on update failure is unspecified and thus left unmodeled.
TariffEngine.price is implemented within this module using DT-P rules; no separate external engine behavior needs to be modeled beyond the required interface.
NotificationService methods may raise exceptions to signal delivery failure, and such exceptions must be swallowed so that the response and stored quote remain unchanged.
ScreeningService.screen returns an integer risk_index on success and raises ScreeningUnavailableError specifically to represent the “screening outage” branch; no other error modes are modeled.
QuoteStore.store_draft returns a string quote_id on success and raises StoreUnavailableError on storage failure; no other failure signaling mechanism is modeled.
Request field type validation is performed in Python using isinstance checks against (int, float) for numeric fields and str for shipper_id, in addition to the numeric bounds from DT-V.

claims.text: Validation per DT-V happens before anything else; invalid requests are rejected immediately with status "rejected: invalid_request" and no draft storage, screening, pricing, or notification occurs.
On storage failure, the response status is "error: store_unavailable" and nothing else runs: no screening, no pricing, no notification.
On screening outage the quote is still priced per DT-P, stored with status "held_unscreened", not notified, and the response carries the price and hold: true.

Screening decisions map risk_index bands to outcomes: <=41 → quoted with price and quote document; 42–66 → review_hold without price or notification; >=67 → refused_screening without price but with refusal notice.
Pricing DT-P specifies: base = 0.87*weight_kg + 1.13*distance_km; if weight_kg>1244 add 316; if distance_km>=4912 multiply running total by 1.19; final price is round(result, 2).
Notification is fire-and-forget: any delivery failure never changes the stored quote or the response.

The overall flow order is: validate, store draft, screen, apply DT-S, price where DT-S marks priced, notify where DT-S marks notified, return response, with the special branch for screening outage pricing and held_unscreened.
The API response includes quote_id whenever a draft was stored, price only on priced rows, and hold: true only on held_unscreened.
